objective: Stop treating title and poster as separate repair tasks. Create one coherent visual concept in which a non-generic custom 茶作 wordmark, photography, support typography and negative space are designed as one poster system; rebuild it in Figma only after the visual direction is accepted.
diagnosis_to_fix: generic brush-calligraphy title with insufficient proprietary structure
photo + headline + caption stacking rather than a designed poster system

five_high_leverage_variables.name: custom_wordmark_identity
five_high_leverage_variables.target: 茶作 must retain immediate readability but introduce brand-specific structural decisions beyond brush calligraphy: proprietary terminals, internal cuts/joins, unequal mass and designed negative space.

five_high_leverage_variables.name: title_photo_interlock
five_high_leverage_variables.target: The title must interact with photographic subject/empty field rather than simply sit above the photo.

five_high_leverage_variables.name: poster_attention_geometry
five_high_leverage_variables.target: Use one decisive asymmetrical composition with a clear visual anchor and secondary counterweight; avoid one-column text stacking.

five_high_leverage_variables.name: support_hierarchy
five_high_leverage_variables.target: English/Chinese support copy must form a deliberate typographic system with the title, not merely captions underneath.

five_high_leverage_variables.name: tonal_negative_space_system
five_high_leverage_variables.target: Use crop, tonal control and empty-space allocation to create poster tension without adding decorative clutter.

workflow: Produce one holistic poster-direction concept first; do not separately optimize the wordmark in isolation.
Human actual-pixel review of overall poster and custom wordmark.
Only if accepted, reconstruct the accepted concept in Figma with editable wordmark/vector, typography, crop/alignment and tonal structure.
Then perform formal P6 export and full-poster validation.
